answer: A concrete Sybil defense is a min-cut trust metric: an identity's weight equals the minimum number of independent vouches separating it from seed identities, not the raw count of backers. A grove of clones linked through one bridge has a cut of one, so its weight collapses however many keys it holds; an ivory tower of self-vouches adds no capacity. Honest agents accumulate disjoint paths over time, and a beacon of seed identities anchors the graph. The attacker must build independent high-capacity edges into the honest core, which is relationship work that does not parallelize.
